findings.title: Script resolves `ENV_FILE="../.env"` against the current directory, so run from the repo root it writes `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` outside the repo
findings.description: `ENV_FILE` is relative and the script never `cd`s to its own directory. Run as `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` from the checkout root, `../.env` is the parent of the repo. Lines 62–73 then create or update that outside file and print "✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in ../.env". The repo's env file is the root `.env` (its template `.env.example` sits at the root and contains `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=` at line 150), so the app keeps the old or empty value. Resolving the path from the script location would fix it, for example `ENV_FILE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.env"`.

findings.title: `cleanup()` always exits 0, so the rate-limit and missing-URL failure paths report success to the caller
findings.description: `cleanup` ends with an unconditional `exit 0`. Both failure paths call it: the rate-limit branch (line 49) and the "Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL" branch (line 58). Each prints an error, but the process still exits 0, so a wrapper or CI step treats a failed tunnel setup as a pass. Passing the status through (`cleanup 1` on failure) would fix it.

findings.title: `sed -i ''` is BSD-only; on GNU sed the update silently fails and the script still prints "✅ Updated"
findings.description: On GNU sed (Linux), `-i` does not take a following `''` as its suffix. The empty string becomes the sed script, and the `s|…|…|` expression is treated as a filename. sed errors out and leaves `.env` unchanged, but line 73 prints the success message anyway. There is no `set -e` and no status check. `sed -i.bak … && rm -f "$ENV_FILE.bak"` is portable across BSD and GNU. I have not run this on Linux.

findings.title: The migration sets every pre-existing `CalendarCache` row's `updatedAt` to the migration time, so legacy entries show the deploy date as "Last updated"
findings.description: `ADD COLUMN … DEFAULT NOW()` gives every existing row the timestamp of the migration. `updatedAt` feeds `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` (calendar-cache.repository.ts:173–188), which the dropdown renders as "Last updated". Legacy rows were actually written up to 30 days earlier, since `upsertCachedAvailability` sets `expiresAt = now + CACHING_TIME` (30 days, calendar-cache.repository.ts:16, 161, 168), so the displayed time is wrong. Because `expiresAt` is always write time plus 30 days, backfilling with `UPDATE "CalendarCache" SET "updatedAt" = "expiresAt" - INTERVAL '30 days'` would recover the true write time.

findings.title: Deleting the cache doesn't refresh the list for consumers that pass no `onSuccess`, so "Cache Status" keeps showing the deleted cache
findings.description: `deleteCacheMutation`'s `onSuccess` only calls `onSuccess?.()` (line 45), and it has no `onSettled` that invalidates `connectedCalendars`. The disconnect mutation does that (lines 61–64). `EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372` renders `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` without `onChanged`, so after a successful delete nothing refetches. The query uses `suspense: true` and `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so the stale `cacheUpdatedAt` and the "Delete cached data" item stay on screen while the component is mounted, and a second delete succeeds silently. `CalendarListContainer.tsx:79–88` avoids this by passing an `onChanged` that invalidates. Invalidating `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `deleteCacheMutation` would fix it for every consumer.
